question: Which of the following helps in the absorption and upward movement of water and minerals dissolved in it from roots to the leaves?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Transpiration**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Transpiration is the process by which water evaporates from the surface of plant leaves, creating a negative pressure that pulls water upward from the roots through the xylem.
 
• This process helps in the absorption and upward movement of water and minerals dissolved in it from the roots to the leaves.
 
• It plays a crucial role in maintaining the water balance and nutrient distribution within the plant.
 
• The continuous movement of water helps in the cooling of the plant and also enables the uptake of essential nutrients from the soil.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Xylem**

 
 
• Xylem is a type of vascular tissue in plants responsible for the transport of water and nutrients from the roots to other parts of the plant.
 
• It consists of various types of cells, including tracheids and vessel elements, which are specialized for water conduction.
 
 
 
• **Stomata**
 
 
• Stomata are small openings on the surface of leaves and stems that facilitate gas exchange and transpiration.
 
• They are surrounded by guard cells that regulate their opening and closing.
 
 
 
• **Root Hair**
 
 
• Root hairs are extensions of root epidermal cells that increase the surface area for water and mineral absorption from the soil.
 
 
 
• **Cohesion-Tension Theory**
 
 
• This theory explains the mechanism of water movement in plants, where cohesion between water molecules and tension created by transpiration drive the upward movement of water.
